## Summary
- Route any review `HUMAN_DECISION` handoff to `agent-self-approve` when self-approval is enabled, including non-`SHIP` verdicts.
- Pass source verdict/recommended-step/context into self-approval prompts and keep deterministic approval restricted to trusted current-head `SHIP` provenance.
- Relax self-approval preflight to allow trusted current-head non-`SHIP` synthesis as a decision gate while preserving resolver approval safeguards.
- Update docs and regression coverage for non-`SHIP` `HUMAN_DECISION` routing, preflight, and prompt rendering.

## Verification
- `npm --prefix .agent run build`
- `node --test .agent/dist/__tests__/handoff.test.js .agent/dist/__tests__/dispatch-agent-orchestrator-cli.test.js .agent/dist/__tests__/orchestrate-handoff-cli.test.js .agent/dist/__tests__/self-approval.test.js .agent/dist/__tests__/prepare-self-approve-cli.test.js .agent/dist/__tests__/envelope.test.js`
- `node --test .agent/dist/__tests__/envelope.test.js`
- `git diff --check`

Note: full `npm --prefix .agent test` currently fails on this checkout because `.agent/sepo-version.json` is absent (`committed Sepo version metadata validates`), after all touched tests pass.

Follow-up for #262 / https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/262#issuecomment-4471162486.

> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue
- PR #265 is stacked on PR #262 and broadens the review handoff so any review synthesis with `Recommended Next Step = HUMAN_DECISION` can route to `agent-self-approve` when self-approval is enabled.
- It preserves the deterministic resolver guard that actual GitHub approval still requires trusted current-head `SHIP` provenance.
- It improves on PR #264 by passing source verdict, recommended next step, and handoff context into the self-approval prompt.
- The remaining gaps are policy wording and preflight scope around when non-`SHIP` self-approval is allowed to run.

## Review
The core route is mostly correct, and the live stacked head already has the workflow wiring and disabled-stop return that one reviewer flagged as missing. However, the current prompt/docs still preserve a normal “send this back to a human” outcome, and the relaxed preflight is broader than the requested `HUMAN_DECISION` decision-gate path.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| HUMAN_DECISION still has a normal human fallback | BLOCKING | [`handoff.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/ae6c65407965d10627bb46826f3a4284d72aa963/.agent/src/handoff.ts#L89-L92), [`agent-self-approve.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/ae6c65407965d10627bb46826f3a4284d72aa963/.github/prompts/agent-self-approve.md#L28-L32), and docs still say to block for a human decision. That conflicts with the #264 follow-up direction that self-approval should make the decision when enabled. |
| Non-SHIP preflight is relaxed for all self-approval runs | WARNING | [`prepare-self-approve.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/ae6c65407965d10627bb46826f3a4284d72aa963/.agent/src/cli/prepare-self-approve.ts#L92-L97) now uses `requireShip: false` unconditionally. Approval remains protected later, but manual or accidental non-`HUMAN_DECISION` self-approval runs can now spend an agent run outside the intended route. |

## Progress
- Existing PR discussion already acknowledges the human-fallback wording concern in the rubrics review.
- Posted one inline comment for the unscoped preflight relaxation: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/265#discussion_r3255269940
- No replies were added, no comments were minimized, and no review threads were resolved.
- One reviewer’s missing `agent-orchestrator.yml` wiring and fall-through concerns were not carried forward: the live stacked head includes `source_recommended_next_step` wiring and an explicit `HUMAN_DECISION` disabled stop.

## Issue Details
<details>
<summary>HUMAN_DECISION still has a normal human fallback</summary>

**Cause:** The implementation routes `HUMAN_DECISION` to self-approval, but the generated context and self-approval prompt still describe “block for a human decision” / “decision should stay with a human” as an ordinary outcome.

**Candidate solutions:** Reword runtime context, prompt, docs, and tests so self-approval decides: `REQUEST_CHANGES` for concrete follow-up, `APPROVE` only for trusted current-head `SHIP`, and `BLOCKED` only for safety, missing-context, or automation-failure cases.

**Comments:** This is not an approval-bypass issue; the resolver safeguard remains intact. The concern is that the agent behavior still permits the exact fallback the requester asked to remove.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Non-SHIP preflight is relaxed for all self-approval runs</summary>

**Cause:** `prepare-self-approve.ts` passes `requireShip: false` without checking whether the workflow was launched from a review `HUMAN_DECISION` handoff.

**Candidate solutions:** Pass `source_recommended_next_step` into the prepare step and use `requireShip: false` only when it normalizes to `human_decision`; keep the old `SHIP` preflight for ordinary/manual self-approval runs. Add a focused regression test for a non-`SHIP`, non-`HUMAN_DECISION` run stopping in preflight.

**Comments:** Actual approval is still blocked by resolver provenance checks, so this is a scope/control-flow issue rather than a privilege escalation.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
FIX_PR: the remaining issues are concrete branch changes in prompt/docs/preflight wiring and are safe for an automated fix-pr pass.

## Final Verdict
NEEDS_REWORK

## Action Items
- [ ] Remove normal “human decision” fallback wording from self-approval context, prompts, docs, and tests; reserve `BLOCKED` for safety, missing-context, or automation-failure cases.
- [ ] Scope `requireShip: false` in self-approval preflight to review `HUMAN_DECISION` handoffs and add regression coverage.

This can run self-approval for a non-`HUMAN_DECISION` non-`SHIP` synthesis via stale/manual input, though actual approval remains protected. |

## Issue Details
<details>
<summary>Trusted synthesis recommended step is not verified</summary>

**Cause:** `prepare-self-approve.ts` derives `isHumanDecisionGate` only from the workflow input `SOURCE_RECOMMENDED_NEXT_STEP`, then passes `requireShip: !isHumanDecisionGate`. The provenance function validates trusted actor, current head, and verdict, but when `requireShip === false` it accepts any latest trusted current-head verdict without checking that the synthesis recommended `HUMAN_DECISION`.

**Candidate solutions:** Extend trusted synthesis parsing to extract `Recommended Next Step`, and allow non-`SHIP` preflight only when the latest trusted current-head synthesis itself says `HUMAN_DECISION`. Add a regression test where the workflow input says `HUMAN_DECISION` but the trusted synthesis says `FIX_PR` or `NO_AUTOMATED_ACTION`, and preflight stops.

**Comments:** This is not an approval bypass; the resolver still refuses actual approval without trusted current-head `SHIP`. The issue is delegated route control and avoiding unintended self-approval agent runs.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Optional prompt and coverage polish</summary>

**Cause:** `defaultReviewSelfApprovalHandoffContext()` repeats `HUMAN_DECISION` in consecutive sentences, `source_conclusion` can render lowercase in the prompt, and one prior `REQUEST_CHANGES` provenance variant is no longer explicitly tested.

**Candidate solutions:** Trim the duplicate context prefix, render verdicts consistently, and consider retaining both trusted and untrusted `REQUEST_CHANGES` test variants.

**Comments:** These are polish items only; they should not drive automation unless touched alongside the required provenance fix.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
FIX_PR: the remaining warning has a concrete, focused branch change and regression test path suitable for automated repair.

## Final Verdict
MINOR_ISSUES
